chunks: God presents an example of two men: one dumb, unable to do a thing, and a burden on his master; wherever he sends him, he returns without any good. Could he be equal to one who enjoins what is just, and follows the right path?

key_terms.كَلٌّ: A burden, one who consumes resources without contributing

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the two men in Surah An-Nahl verse 76?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this parable (mathal) from Surah An-Nahl (16:76) is often interpreted as a contrast between the idolaters, who are spiritually 'mute' and burdened by their false deities, and the monotheists or Imams who actively guide humanity to justice. The 'mute' figure represents those whose faith is passive and derivative, while the 'enjoining justice' figure embodies the active, authoritative role of the Prophet and the Ahl al-Bayt in conveying divine truth. This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on the necessity of both correct belief and active leadership (Imamah) for spiritual success.
